summary: Not a fire lookout: a 60-foot steel observation tower at the Oak Island Coast Guard Station, Brunswick County. No story; proposed hidden for editor review.

corrections.why: A Coast Guard station observation tower used to watch the sea and river, not a wildland fire lookout. NGS calls it an OAK ISLAND CG LOOKOUT TOWER, and the HABS record ties its use to monitoring waters. DESIGN.md keeps non-fire towers hidden.

notes_for_editor: No story written, following the Hawaii coastal-artillery precedent in the story guide: this is a Coast Guard station observation tower, not a wildland fire lookout, so it is proposed hidden for a human decision. If you want it kept as a Coast Guard lookout, a story can be written from the NGS datasheet (first observed 1962, recovered in good condition 1964) and the HABS record (NC-401). In the HABS passages I checked, no build or removal date for the tower appears. The NGS datasheet, the tnlandforms NC list (NCT222, DD 2461) and the HABS record are the only sources. Brief status unknown; the NGS sheet gives no later recovery note.
